summary.text: No network publishes a self-serve way for a prospective issuer, acquirer or ATM operator to see its price. Every route ends in a form, a mailbox or an account executive.
Of the four, only Visa was found to publish licensing steps, tools and review criteria for a new issuer or acquirer before any contact.
Banks and credit unions often evaluate networks through paid negotiators who run bids between Visa and Mastercard for incentives.
The only neutral cross-network comparison found is the Fed's debit interchange table, and the Fed warns it does not show what any issuer would earn.
Participants told the RBA that confidentiality terms stop them comparing network prices or understanding their own bills.
Discover's strongest evaluation assets sit with PULSE: a named team, a portfolio review, switcher case studies and an ABA endorsement with a due diligence report.
For fintechs, Visa and Mastercard run named programmes with directories of enablers, while Discover's fintech page names no processor, sponsor bank or programme manager.
Four of six issuing platforms checked document no Discover issuing, and a fintech guide drops Discover and Amex from the network choice altogether.
Developers can judge Mastercard and Visa from open documentation and a free sandbox, while Discover's Developer Center admits developers only by invitation.
Selling is often done by third parties the networks arm: Amex gives OptBlue sales agents an objection guide and comparative spend data.
Evaluation pages go stale: Visa's Fast Track cites a 2022 fact sheet and Amex's issuer page a 2022 ranking.

how_it_works.text: A prospect first emails a regional licensing team, then receives Visa Access credentials once Visa confirms eligibility.
The application is completed in the Client Lifecycle Management tool under a temporary UVID, and approval issues a final Business ID.
Visa publishes the four review areas: regulatory permissions, AML and ATF programmes, credit and settlement risk, and risk management.
Principal clients are pitched as larger institutions working directly with Visa on product and marketing, and paying service fees whose amounts are unpublished.
Economics are negotiated. Visa recorded 15.75 billion dollars of client incentives in fiscal 2025 and amortises up-front payments over each contract.
Visa Consulting and Analytics sells advisory work to issuers, including portfolio migration results.
Visa Payments Forum is Visa's largest annual client and partner event.

design_moves.title: An evaluation pack per partner type
partner_types: Issuers: community banks and credit unions
design_moves.move: Give each prospect a downloadable pack: participation model, fee structure lines, service levels the network commits to, ownership separation terms and endorsements.
design_moves.why_advantage: Banks already buy due diligence from ABA and advisers. A network that supplies it first shortens their work and sets the terms of comparison.

design_moves.title: A self-serve debit yield model
partner_types: Issuers: community banks and credit unions
design_moves.move: Turn the Debit Advantage Analysis into a model a prospect runs on its own mix, showing exempt yield after routing with its assumptions visible.
design_moves.why_advantage: Visa publishes exempt rates and runs a public calculator. Discover hides yield behind a call, and the Fed table cannot answer an issuer's own case.

design_moves.title: One front door that names the next step
partner_types: Issuers: community banks and credit unions
design_moves.move: Replace scattered forms and mailboxes with one intake that routes by partner type, states the next step, who owns it and the committed reply time.
design_moves.why_advantage: Rivals end in newsletter forms, mailboxes or representatives. A clear first step with a committed response time would stand out.

design_moves.title: A provider shelf for fintechs
design_moves.move: Publish the processors, sponsor banks and programme managers that carry the network, by product and country, and start the fintech path inside one of them.
design_moves.why_advantage: Visa and Mastercard win fintechs through enabler directories. Discover names none, so fintechs never see it as an option.

design_moves.title: Arm the channel that sells
design_moves.move: Give acquirers, ISOs and ATM processors a seller kit with merchant-level value evidence and objection answers, modelled on the OptBlue hub pattern.
design_moves.why_advantage: Merchants ask what volume a network brings. Amex answers through sellers, while Discover's pages give no spend figure.

design_moves.title: Price visible to a stranger
partner_types: Issuers: community banks and credit unions
design_moves.move: Show a standard acquirer schedule and fee structure before sign-up, as Discover already does in Canada, with incentives on a separate line.
design_moves.why_advantage: No major US network publishes the network fees a prospect would pay. Interac and eftpos do, and the RBA is forcing publication in Australia.

design_moves.title: Open evaluation for developers
design_moves.move: Make specifications, sandbox keys and a pricing model page available before any representative contact, with markdown twins for assistants.
design_moves.why_advantage: Mastercard and Visa already allow this, so Discover's invite-only door removes it from developer shortlists.

design_moves.title: Dated proof from peers
partner_types: Issuers: community banks and credit unions
design_moves.move: Carry case studies and client survey quotes by partner type, each dated and sourced, and keep every headline figure current.
design_moves.why_advantage: Visa and PULSE use peer case studies, while Visa and Amex pages show figures years old. Fresh proof reads as care.
